title: Descent planning
summary: Ten thousand feet to lose before Kennedy: start down at the right distance and cross 15 DME at 5,000 ft.
briefing: Fifteen thousand feet, fifty-eight miles south-west of Kennedy, heading for the VOR. We have to cross fifteen DME at five thousand feet.
The rule of thumb: three miles for every thousand feet to lose. Ten thousand feet is thirty miles, so we start down at about forty-five DME, a little more to slow down.

tasks.goal: Cross 15 DME from Kennedy at 5,000 ft.
tasks.say: Set five thousand in the altitude window. At about forty-five DME, start down: the vertical speed mode, Y, and around eighteen hundred feet a minute.
tasks.sayGlass: Set five thousand in the altitude window. At about forty-five DME, start down: flight level change, J, or vertical speed, Y, at around eighteen hundred feet a minute.

cues.say: We're getting fast: shallower, or the speed brake.

debrief.three: Right on the altitude at the fix. That's a descent planned, not guessed.
debrief.two: Close. Check the sums as you go down: three miles a thousand feet.
debrief.one: We made the fix, off the altitude. Start down earlier, or later, and keep checking.
debrief.failed: That descent didn't come together. Three miles for every thousand feet. Again?
